memory_update.text: WEST is the highest-priority underfollowed candidate for the coffee/tea/extract/private-label foodservice node because filings directly tie it to foodservice and restaurant customers plus extract and RTD capacity.

FARM is a high-relevance but high-risk speculative shadow candidate: filings support DSD, equipment service, and restaurant/foodservice customers, but market cap and turnaround risk place it below the preferred size threshold.

HBB is a below-$300M speculative equipment candidate whose commercial restaurant, fast-food, bar, hotel, coffee maker, and specialty beverage equipment exposure needs revenue-materiality verification.

For this node, the most Serenity-relevant chokepoints appear to be extraction/RTD capacity, green-coffee sourcing and commodity management, direct-store-delivery route density, equipment service uptime, and customer-specific beverage formulation.
Need a separate pass for private-label beverage and tea manufacturers such as TreeHouse Foods if it remains publicly listed and sufficiently exposed after any take-private or portfolio changes.

summary: Expanded the universe around behind-the-scenes coffee, tea, extract, beverage-equipment, and route-service chokepoints for restaurants and foodservice. The strongest underfollowed public-market matches are Westrock Coffee for custom coffee/tea/extract solutions and Farmer Bros. for DSD coffee, tea, allied products, and equipment service. Hamilton Beach Brands and Middleby broaden the node into commercial beverage equipment, coffee/beverage dispensing, and foodservice equipment infrastructure. This pass intentionally avoids consumer-brand-only names except as context; each candidate still needs filing-level follow-up on restaurant/customer exposure, margin sensitivity to green coffee and freight, leverage, and whether beverage equipment exposure is material enough to matter.
